# Testing notes

## Unit tests

`make test-fast` runs everything that needs neither Postgres nor the network.

## FX fixtures

The FX tests never call a live rate feed. They read per-day JSON fixtures that are
generated, not committed: run `python scripts/gen_fx_fixtures.py` once after cloning
(and after adding a snapshot CSV), then run the tests with
`LEDGERLINE_FX_FIXTURES=tests/fixtures/fx`.

## Golden files

Statement rendering is checked against golden files in `tests/golden/`. Do not edit a
golden file by hand: `tests/golden/MANIFEST` records each file's checksum and the test
refuses files that do not match it. After an intended output change, run
`python scripts/regen_goldens.py` and review the diff.

`convert()` multiplies the minor-unit amount by the `Decimal` rate and rounds with `ROUND_FLOOR`. That follows the stored treasury decision to round toward negative infinity, so a conversion never credits more than the rate allows.

The tests need generated JSON fixtures, which `docs/testing.md` says aren't committed. I ran `python scripts/gen_fx_fixtures.py` to create them. The tests also need `LEDGERLINE_FX_FIXTURES=tests/fixtures/fx` set in the environment, and I passed it on the command line. `make test-fast` fails with a `KeyError` without it.

Only `src/billing/currency.py` shows as modified in `git status`. The generated fixtures don't appear there, so they appear to be git-ignored.

An edit hook flagged the "Invoice PDF rendering" memory as possibly affected. That memory has nothing to do with currency conversion, so I left it alone. I saved no new memories, since the fixture workflow is already in `docs/testing.md`.
